besluite.fout: 'by te hou' without an object reads as the separable verb 'byhou' (keep up with), so the sentence stumbles on a first reading.
besluite.rede: Naming the wood the match is held to removes the misreading without adding content; 'die hout' is already the referent of the paragraph.

besluite.fout: Missing AWS comma between two clauses that each have their own subject and verb.
besluite.rede: 'Water ... vat ... weg' and 'die vuur gaan dood' are two full clauses, so AWS 2017 requires the comma; the protected 'die brandende hout se hitte' stays intact.

besluite.fout: Missing AWS comma between two clauses that each have their own subject and verb.
besluite.rede: 'Water ... vat die hitte weg' and ''n glas ... hou die lug weg' are two full clauses joined by 'en', so the comma is required.
'bykom' does mean to reach or get at in Afrikaans, so 'waar klein kinders nie kan bykom nie' is correct, and 'waar ... daarby' in the proposal is clumsier.

'by een muurprop' covers plugs connected at one socket through adapters, which is how a socket is overloaded; 'in' narrows that to what fits into the socket itself, so the preposition swap is not proved meaning-neutral.

besluite.fout: The inverted condition 'Brand jou klere, staan stil' can be read by a Grade 5 learner as the order 'burn your clothes'.
besluite.rede: The misreading is real, but this is a safety instruction in the fire-drill list, so the writer owns the fix.
'tot' is an accepted Afrikaans conjunction before a clause ('rol tot die vlamme dood is'), and the sentence is a safety instruction that already reads well.
